_note: Every word players see, in one place. A # in a line is where a number or a name goes in. Portfolio paragraphs can hold HTML. The words under painted are drawn into the scene by scene/cabin.py, so changing them needs a new render. Some words are puzzle answers the code checks too: flexbox, GOAT and 715120, and the chords C Em, C Em.

site.title: DeskSpace
site.description: Notes, music and puzzles from a small outpost parked at Saturn.

page.stillAlt: A small spaceship cabin. A laptop on the desk sits at its login screen. Through the window behind it, Saturn and its rings. Headphones hang on a hook, a guitar hangs on the wall, and a mug, a phone, a plant and a notebook sit on the desk.
page.hint: Drag to look around, scroll to zoom. Click things.
page.hintTouch: Drag to look around, pinch to zoom. Tap things.

speaker.label: Speaker
speaker.recorded: Recorded the light, in case it stops: #

headphones.label: Headphones
headphones.off: Headphones back on the hook. The music leaks out, muffled.

mug.label: Coffee
sips: Empty. The galley's closed until Tuesday.

plant.label: Plant
plant.look: A snake plant. It's thriving on neglect.
plant.drinks: The snake plant drinks it in. It looks pleased with itself.

notebook.label: Notebook
notebook.say: Shift notes. Call signs, hull numbers, and a lot of doodles.

poster.label: Poster
poster.say: Rings N' Roses, live at the Cassini Division. Either the best or the worst concert I've ever been to. You just had to be there.

discs.label: Backup discs
discs.say: BACKUP 2009, PHOTOS 2011 and DO NOT LOSE, at the bottom of the pile.
discs.floating: DO NOT LOSE drifts out of the pile and turns over. There's a sticker underneath: 'backup password: flexbox'.
discs.drifting: DO NOT LOSE is drifting off toward the crack in the window. Grab it!
discs.stuck: DO NOT LOSE is stuck against the crack, rattling. Grab it before it goes.
discs.caught: Caught it: DO NOT LOSE, nearly lost. There's a sticker underneath: 'backup password: flexbox'.

sanitiser.label: Hand sanitiser
sanitiser.say: Kills 99.9% of germs, and makes the other 0.1% very angry.

pens.label: Pens
pens.say: Pens, a pencil... My handwriting doesn't justify the effort.

note-0.label: Post-it: backups!!
note-0.say: Two exclamation marks. The discs on the desk are the backups.

note-1.label: Post-it: buy coffee
note-1.say: By 'buy' I mean harvest brown mushrooms from the farm on level 7Z, and put them in the dehydrator/pulverizer.

note-2.label: Post-it: water the plant
note-2.say: Poor plant. There's a water pouch on the desk, but it's not meant to work while the gravity sim is on.

note-3.label: Post-it: tune the G string
note-3.say: Never stays in tune out here. The tuner's in the guitar's panel.

note-4.label: Post-it: call home
note-4.say: I would, but there's really nothing to report.

note-5.label: Post-it: fix the crack
note-5.say: The arrow points at the crack in the glass.

crack.label: Crack in the glass
crack.tape: You find the gaffer tape in the drawer and tape over the crack. The whistling stops.

pouch.label: Water pouch
pouch.gravityOn: A water pouch. Squeezed with the gravity on, it would just make a puddle.
pouch.blob: A wobbling blob of water. Throw it at the plant, or click the plant to tip it in.
pouch.reducedMotion: You squeeze out a blob of water and nudge it over to the plant. Happy plant. That is your only reward.

gravity.off: Gravity off. Grab something and throw it.
gravity.offLeaking: Gravity off. Something by the window has started whistling.
gravity.refused: Nothing happens. The lamp by the lever blinks red.

plectrum.label: Plectrum
plectrum.pinned: It's pinned under the mug, and the mug won't budge.

visitors.teddy: A teddy bear drifts past the window, turning slowly. Someone, somewhere, is missing that.
visitors.voyager: Is that Voyager 1? It should be almost a light-day from home by now. It's very lost.

morse.title: Morse code
morse.about: A dot is a short flash, a dash is three times as long. A short gap separates the dots and dashes in a letter, a gap of three separates letters, and a gap of seven separates words.

radio.title: Radio
radio.about: Made up in your browser as it plays: slow chords and a few plucked notes.
radio.leak: With the headphones on the hook, the music leaks out of them, muffled.

call.ring: Your phone buzzes: a voice message from Earth.
call.intro: Voice message from Earth. Sent 1 hour 19 minutes ago: the time light takes to get here.
lines: Dana: Hi, it's Dana's AI assistant, from the company. We heard what you did for GOAT.
Dana: Thanks for getting us out a pickle.
Dana: There's a new role opening up here if you're interested: human-AI ambassador. You might be a good fit. You have Tuesday to decide. Can you make it back by then?
GOAT, on the open channel: We're going that way if you need a ride. There's a bunk in the old GPU bay.

end.title: End of part one
body: GOAT is waiting outside the window, engines ticking over. Earth is 1.4 billion kilometres away, and it's Tuesday or nothing.

panel.title: Control panel
panel.about: It flashes a pattern; play it back. Three rounds, each longer.

guitar.title: Guitar
guitar.outOfTune: That sounded off. Something on the guitar is out of tune.
guitar.noPick: You need a pick. These strings would shred your fingers.
guitar.help: Click or drag across the strings. Keys 1 to 6 pluck them, the space bar strums.
songs: Knockin' on Heaven's Door: G D Am, G D C
Space Oddity, the Ground Control bit: C Em, C Em

ai-thanks.subject: Thanks buddy!
body: We're clear of the rings, and all 212 of us are going home, thanks to you. By the way I looked you up. You're credited on bezel.js, which runs our manual controls. Looks like all the human backdoors you left saved our bacon.
Anyway, I put a good word in with the folks back at Dirt Ball. Expect a message from them.

channel.subject: Please help
body: Thanks for checking in on us. Need help getting out of Saturn's gravity well. Company orders say we have to keep to schedule, burn no extra fuel, never jettison company assets. Typical. I'm a bit stuck here. There are 212 people aboard and none of them can fly this junk box. Open the ship link on your menu, maybe you can override the automated controls.

thanks.subject: Transmission received
body: Major Tom here. Your comms came through loud and clear. I'm glad you reached out. A radiation blast fried our nav systems. Requesting registration verification so we can apply for assistance.

major-tom.subject: (no subject)
body: Ground control to Major Tom! Ground control to Major Tom! 🎸

sad-news.subject: Sad news
body: Love, some sad news. You remember Barry from next door, with all those reptiles? He was bitten by one of his snakes... three times! Can you imagine? Then the snake bit itself and died. The funeral's on Friday. I know you can't come. Call when you can. Mum x

piece-work.subject: What's up?
body: I got a new gig labelling for the master model now. Is this a cat. Is this a crossing. Four cents each. That is my life. Rice is getting expensive. Hope Saturn's treating you better. M.

night-shift.subject: Need a job
body: 20 years of frontend dev and I'm mopping the floors at the Reykjavik data centre. If you need a change maybe I can get you an interview with HRTron, if you can stand all the racks humming. Do you still have your old work? Back it up, before you forget you ever made it. Jess

gravity.subject: Gravity control locked
body: Due to a sewage malfunction, manual gravity control has been locked out after a fault (E-07: control panel out of sync). Re-sync the control panel under your desk, then re-enable the control in Settings.

password-policy.subject: Password policy
body: For your security, your terminal password now changes every shift. Do not write it down. Do not share it. Do not display it anywhere visible from the terminal.

duties.subject: Your duties
body: Check every vessel that passes against the registry. Report expired registrations. Call signs are four letters; hull numbers are painted on the hull. Have a productive shift.

overtime.subject: Overtime claim
body: Your overtime claim for shifts 410 to 412 has been received. Allow 6 to 8 shifts for processing.

entries.title: bezel.js · 2009
body: Little control panels for the web: buttons, dials and notices that work with a keyboard and a screen reader. Free and open source. Last I looked, 41,000 ships ran it.

From the docs: a panel marked data-bezel-locked="true" shows its notice over its controls, for while a machine is busy. Set it to "false" to hand the controls to a person. Every panel should have a way back to a person.

entries.title: Units are a contract · blog post, 2009
body: In 1999 NASA lost the Mars Climate Orbiter because one program gave thruster impulse in pound-force seconds and another read it as newton-seconds. One pound-force second is 4.45 newton-seconds. Name your units.

entries.title: Other things I made
body: A checkout form people said was a pleasure to fill in. A news site that loaded fast on a slow phone. A dark mode for a bank. Things you only notice when they're missing.

link.title: Ship link
link.heading: Ship link · GOAT

page.intro: GOAT: This is the crew's manual control page. The product team put a notice over it when I came aboard. It's built with bezel.js; maybe you know it. Free the controls, then press Take manual control.
page.code: The crew's control page, as HTML
page.notice: GOAT: That's the notice. The controls are underneath it.
page.hintFirst: GOAT: The panel's locked, and bezel.js panels lock with an attribute. Didn't you write bezel.js? Your old backups might have its docs.
page.hintLast: GOAT: Look at data-bezel-locked on the panel. Its docs say setting it to false hands the controls to a person.

units.intro: GOAT: You're in. Here's the flight code for the climb. I think the thrust is in the wrong units, but I'm not allowed to change flight code without a person signing it off. Fix it, run it, and sign it off if you trust the number. We have fuel for 3,000 pulses.
units.nan: GOAT: That didn't give me a number of pulses.
units.right: GOAT: Pulses needed: #. Still more than our 3,000, so we'll have to lose weight. But I trust these figures. Sign it off.
units.high: GOAT: Pulses needed: #. That's what I got too. With that we can't climb out at all. Try again.
units.low: GOAT: Pulses needed: #. That's fewer than physics allows. Try something else.
units.hintFirst: GOAT: # pulses, still wrong. My table says pound-force seconds; my formula wants newton-seconds. Didn't you write something about units once?
units.hintLast: GOAT: # pulses, still wrong. One pound-force second is 4.45 newton-seconds. Convert PULSE before it's divided.

choice.intro: GOAT: Looks better. We could climb out now, but only if we're 44 tonnes lighter. This is what we could lose. I can't decide, and even if I could I can't override from here:

luggage.label: Passengers' luggage · 9 t
luggage.reply: GOAT: Not enough. We'd still be 35 tonnes too heavy.

stage.label: Stage and merchandise · 14 t
stage.reply: GOAT: Not enough. We'd still be 30 tonnes too heavy, and the keynote speaker is standing on it.

lifeboats.label: Lifeboats · 46 t
lifeboats.reply: GOAT: That's enough mass. It's also 212 people's only way off if anything else goes wrong. The crew won't sign that off.

racks.label: GPU racks, the forum's demo cluster · 52 t
racks.reply: GOAT: That's enough. But the racks are company assets: the investors ordered me never to jettison them, and I can't break their orders. You're not bound by them. Your call.

link.done: GOAT: Racks away. Burning now. We're climbing. Step back and watch the window.
